nodes.label: satteri-docs-test CI job (nextest plus clippy, modelled on rust-test)
nodes.norm_label: satteri-docs-test ci job (nextest plus clippy, modelled on rust-test)
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - bring-satteri-docs-into-ci [ses_f16566313ffegsPu0cbSu1ZZcV].md:L4285] "**`rust-test` (ci.yml:326)** is the primary model: same `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, same `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly`, same `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, same `taiki-e/install-action@cargo-nextest`, same `--no-fail-fast`, same `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER: ""` escape hatch, same `CARGO_PROFILE_{TEST,DEV}_DEBUG: "0"`, same `timeout-minutes` present with a modest value (20 vs its 25)."

The five pre-existing clippy findings are allowed by name rather than fixed, with the stated consequence. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - bring-satteri-docs-into-ci [ses_f16566313ffegsPu0cbSu1ZZcV].md:L4337] "**Consequence, stated plainly:** the job is green on arrival, and the three lint *names* stay open, so a sixth `needless_borrow` anywhere in the crate would also pass. Every other lint is still denied, `dead_code` stays denied, and the comment in the file names all five findings with their exact file locations so the debt is greppable rather than merely non-fatal. I chose this over the alternatives because fixing them means editing `src/layout.rs` and `src/routes/docs.rs`, which the task explicitly placed out of reach, and because a red-on-arrival job is the worst possible outcome for a gap whose whole point is that a green signal was previously meaningless."
